Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co Posts Stable Trade Figures Amid Steady Market Conditions

Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co, the country’s sole petroleum refiner, has reported steady trade figures for the first quarter of 2024, reflecting stable demand and consistent operations across its facilities. The company, a key player in Jordan’s energy sector, processed 1.62 million metric tonnes of crude oil in the quarter, in line with its previous year’s performance for the same period.

According to a statement released by the company on Monday, sales of refined petroleum products—including gasoline, diesel, kerosene, and liquefied petroleum gas—totaled 1.48 million metric tonnes, with domestic demand remaining robust. The company noted that diesel accounted for the largest share of sales, in keeping with market trends observed over the past several years.

“Operational continuity and a reliable supply chain have enabled us to meet the needs of the local market without interruption,” said Fawaz Al-Masri, Chief Operations Officer at Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co. “Our focus remains on maintaining product quality and ensuring a stable supply of energy products to support Jordan’s economy.”

The refinery’s output is primarily consumed domestically, supplying fuel to transportation, industry, and households throughout the country. Imports of crude oil, sourced mainly from regional partners, remained consistent, with no reported logistical issues or supply disruptions.

Local industry analysts say the trade figures reflect the broader stability in Jordan’s energy sector. “Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co has demonstrated operational resilience despite fluctuating global oil prices,” remarked Samer Haddad, an energy analyst at Amman-based consultancy Levant Energy Insights. “These routine trade figures signal that the company is maintaining its role as a steady supplier to the local market.”

The Jordanian government has continued its policy of strategic fuel reserves and moderate subsidies, which have helped shield the market from external volatility. “We have not observed any abnormal price movements or shortages in the domestic market this quarter,” said Reem Suleiman, spokesperson for the Jordan Oil Importers Association. “Refined product inventories have remained within the typical range.”

The company also confirmed ongoing capital investments in maintenance and upgrades at its main facility in Zarqa. A spokesperson indicated that the projects, which include efficiency improvements and environmental upgrades, are proceeding on schedule.

With the broader regional market remaining stable and no major disruptions reported, Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co’s routine trade figures underscore the company’s continued importance in underpinning Jordan’s energy security.
